### Extracted Text

---

**0401240 The Islamic Creed** (3 Credit Hours)  
This course revolves around prophethood, revelation, miracle, belief in angels, the books especially the Qur'an, and destiny. It also touches on the hereafter, evidence on its existence, what happens in it starting with death and partition passing through Judgment Day, wedging, judgment and ending with paradise and hell. It also touches on the topic of the Names and Attributes, its divisions, meanings and the methodologies of scholars in it.

---

**0401311 Analytic Exegesis** (3 Credit Hours)  
This course trains the student on the art of exegesis and its books; it also teaches how to analyze Qur'anic texts from a linguistic and rhetorical point of view. The exegesis of Surat al-Nisa' is a requirement of the course in addition to the meaning of certain vocabularies of the first half of the Qur'an.

---

**0401338 Great figures in intellect and Da’wah** (3 Credit Hours)  
This course aims at highlighting the good model for da'wat by shedding light on a selected group of great figures in intellect and da'wah in Islamic history as well as in the modern world and clarifying their methodologies and manners in calling people to the almighty Allah, and the factors behind their success in tackling the problems of and transcending their communities.

---

**0401339 Methods of Preaching and Teaching** (3 Credit Hours)  
This course aims to introduce the methods of preaching and teaching in mosques. Students will be having practical training (at least 20 sessions a term) in delivering speeches in mosques under the supervision of their teachers.

---

**0401340 Imamah (leadership) and mosque management** (3 Credit Hours)  
This course is about the function of imam, his importance, his role in the community, the conditions required for one to be an imam, his manners, and duties and how he should treat people. The course also touches on mosque management including all buildings, tools, and money it contains.
